messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 SEV-2 opened: Regional degradation (us-east). Symptoms: elevated 5xx + tail latency on /v1/chat and /v1/embeddings. Suspected: network impairment + saturation. IC: Sean Gallagher. Comms: Aisha Bello. War room: #incidents + bridge https://meet.redwoodinference.com/inc-1709669820

Sean Gallagher: IC. Goal is keep service up; consider partial failover to us-west if safe. Miles can you sanity-check routing options? Victor/Harish please advise on DNS + capacity.

Miles Thornton: Yep. Current routing policy for hosted: us-east primary, us-west fallback disabled except manual override. We can flip policy-store to “degraded east -> 25% west” (progressive) OR DNS steer (slower, TTL).

Aisha Bello: Current SLO view: error rate peaked 3.2% on us-east, p99 jumped from ~900ms to 6–8s. us-west looks normal. If we fail over, we need to watch global p99 + queue depth.

Victor Alvarez: DNS: edge record TTL is 60s for api.redwood.ai, but client resolvers can cache longer. Better to do internal routing policy first. DNS steer as last resort.

Harish Reddy: Capacity check: us-west GPU pool headroom is tight. We’re at ~72% util on A100 pool, queue depth trending up already from background jobs. If we shove too much traffic, we’ll just move the problem.

Irene Choi: +1. We can burst some reserved capacity but not instantaneous. Vanessa, can you confirm if any warm spares in us-west can be activated?

Vanessa Ortiz: Looking. We have 12 nodes in “warm standby” (hosted-general) but they’re not fully provisioned with the latest runtime image. ETA to bring online safely: ~25–30 min.

Mina Haddad: Routing side: we can do by-route and by-tier. Proposal: fail over only /v1/chat for free+pro tiers at 10% first. Leave enterprise + embeddings pinned until we see west stability.

Sean Gallagher: That sounds right. Let’s do progressive + scoped. Miles, can you prep the change? Connor, can we treat this as emergency change without the normal release gate?

Connor O'Brien: For incident mitigation yes, but we should keep it reversible + log it. Please post exact policy diff and rollback command in-thread.

Ethan Park: Control plane is healthy. Policy-store write is fine. Just flagging: audit log requires operator token; I can run if needed.

Miles Thornton: I can run with on-call creds. Draft policy change:
- Condition: region_health(us-east)=DEGRADED (5xx>1% for 5m OR p99>4s for 5m)
- Action: route chat traffic: 10% -> us-west for tier in {free, pro}
- Hold-down: 20m, manual override required to go above 50%

Priya Natarajan: Please keep it scoped to the smallest slice that proves improvement. We don’t want to blow up west.

Aisha Bello: Before we flip: confirm west dependencies? Any upstream rate limits? Also we need to tighten timeouts? People reporting client-side timeouts at 10s.

Miles Thornton: West is clean on deps (vector store, token auth). Timeouts: chat upstream currently 30s; we can reduce per-request timeout to 15s to prevent queue buildup, but that’s a separate lever.

Harish Reddy: For west, safe max additional load without paging fleet is ~15% of current east chat QPS. So 10% on free/pro is fine. Please don’t jump to 50%.

Victor Alvarez: If internal routing isn’t enough, DNS steer plan:
1) Lower TTL for api.redwood.ai from 60 -> 30 (but slow effect)
2) Weighted record shift 20% to us-west edge POP
Rollback is trivial but still propagation risk.

Sean Gallagher: OK. Execute internal policy shift first. Stop condition: west queue depth > 2x baseline for >3m OR global 5xx increases. Miles, go ahead.

Miles Thornton: Running change now. Command:
`rrctl policy apply --file chat_failover_10pct_free_pro.yaml --reason "INC-1709669820 mitigate us-east"`

deploy-bot: rrctl: policy apply started by mthornton (INC-1709669820). Target: routing-policy-store/prod. Validation: PASS. Diff: +1 rule, priority=230.

deploy-bot: rrctl: policy apply complete. Propagation: 30-45s.

Aisha Bello: Watching dashboards. Expected: us-east chat QPS drop ~8–12%, west up correspondingly. Also watching global p99.

Mina Haddad: Seeing the route split taking effect. West receiving ~9.4% chat traffic for free/pro. No weirdness on policy evaluator.

Harish Reddy: West GPU util up from 72% -> 78%. Queue depth stable so far (slight bump). Still within safe range.

Aisha Bello: Global 5xx down from 3% -> 1.1% over last 2m. p99 dropped to ~3.5s (still high but improving). us-east remains degraded.

Sean Gallagher: Good. Do we need to go to 20%? Or hold and see if east recovers?

Victor Alvarez: East network loss is still spiky per probes. If we can get another 10% off east it may help; but check west headroom first.

Harish Reddy: 20% may push west >85% util. Risky unless Vanessa brings spares online.

Vanessa Ortiz: Standby nodes are provisioning now. Best case 20 min until they’re in the pool + healthy. I’ll post when ready.

Miles Thornton: Alternative: do 10% more but only for route=/v1/chat AND model family “fast” (quantized) to reduce west compute. That reduces impact on west but adds complexity.

Mina Haddad: We can scope to model tag. But I’d prefer to keep policy simple during incident.

Priya Natarajan: Agree: keep it simple. Let’s not introduce a new dimension mid-incident.

Sean Gallagher: Hold at 10% until spares are online OR east improves. Meanwhile, do validation checks: confirm customer impact on streaming? Also confirm no auth issues due to region change.

Ethan Park: Auth tokens are region-agnostic. But sessions that pin to east via sticky header might still stick. We have some enterprise customers using `x-redwood-region: us-east` hard pin.

Aisha Bello: I’ll ask Support to check for pinned-region tickets. For now, metrics show streaming disconnects reduced slightly but not gone.

Miles Thornton: Post-mitigation verification checklist (please confirm):
1) Global 5xx < 1.5% for 10m
2) Global p99 < 4s for 10m
3) us-west queue depth < 1.5x baseline
4) No sustained burn-rate alerts for Multi-Region Avail SLO
5) Confirm rollback works (`rrctl policy rollback --to PREV`)

Connor O'Brien: +1. Please also capture the exact time we applied the policy so we can correlate in the postmortem.

Miles Thornton: Applied at ~1709670740 (per deploy-bot log).

Vanessa Ortiz: Update: 6/12 standby nodes are healthy, joining west pool now. Remaining ETA ~10 min. That gives more headroom.

Harish Reddy: With 6 nodes added, west util dropped to 70% (nice). We can consider increasing to 20% if east remains bad.

Sean Gallagher: OK, let’s do 20% but keep scope free/pro chat only. Same stop conditions. Miles?

Miles Thornton: Acknowledged. Applying incremental change (10% -> 20%).
`rrctl policy apply --set failover.chat.free_pro.percent=20 --reason "INC-1709669820 increase failover"`

deploy-bot: rrctl: policy apply started by mthornton (INC-1709669820). Validation: PASS. Diff: rule updated.

deploy-bot: rrctl: policy apply complete. Propagation: 30-45s.

Aisha Bello: Observing: global 5xx now 0.6–0.8% last 3m. p99 down to ~2.1s. West queue depth is OK.

Victor Alvarez: Given improvement, I suggest we avoid DNS changes. Keep DNS stable.

Mina Haddad: Routing looks stable at ~19–21% for eligible traffic. No flapping.

Sean Gallagher: Great. Now: post-mitigation validation for 15m. If stable and east recovers, we can dial back gradually.

Aisha Bello: Burn-rate alert has stopped firing; error budget burn back under 2x. Still watching tail latency.

Harish Reddy: Capacity is fine now. But note: if east fully goes down, west cannot take 100% without additional nodes. We should prep a plan.

Irene Choi: Agree. If east worsens, we can:
- shift another 20% (up to 40%) for free/pro chat
- keep enterprise pinned unless approved
- bring remaining standby nodes + request emergency capacity from cloud provider

Ethan Park: Also note: we can enable “graceful shed” on east (429 early) to keep it from timing out. That may improve perceived behavior vs long hangs.

Sean Gallagher: Let’s do that only if timeouts creep up again. For now, stable.

Aisha Bello: Customer impact check: global timeout rate down 60% vs peak. Streaming disconnects down but still above baseline. Likely due to packet loss continuing on east for pinned sessions.

Miles Thornton: For pinned customers, we can reach out to Support/CS to advise removing `x-redwood-region` pin temporarily (if allowed) or switch to multi-region policy.

Sean Gallagher: OK. Marking incident as mitigated pending full recovery. Keep the failover at 20% for the next hour, then reassess.

incident-bot: Status update (IC: sgallagher): Mitigation applied: progressive internal failover for /v1/chat free+pro (20% to us-west). Monitoring for stability. DNS steer not used.

Connor O'Brien: Please don’t forget to add notes to the timeline doc after. Also: once stable, add rollback plan + who approved.

Sean Gallagher: Noted. Approvals: IC (me) + capacity ok by Harish + routing ok by Mina. Will capture in retro.

Aisha Bello: Final check before I drop: all metrics green for last 12m. Will keep an eye for the next 30.

Victor Alvarez: Network probes still show intermittent loss in east (2–4%). NOC engaged.

Sean Gallagher: Thanks all. Leave thread open for updates; ping if any stop conditions hit.
